bibleSpine.kjv: And I saw another angel fly in the midst of heaven, having the everlasting gospel to preach unto them that dwell on the earth, and to every nation, and kindred, and tongue, and people,
bibleSpine.gloss: The everlasting gospel — not a new gospel but the one eternal good news — is the substance of the first angel's message, borne worldwide in the last hour.

bibleSpine.kjv: Saying with a loud voice, Fear God, and give glory to him; for the hour of his judgment is come: and worship him that made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and the fountains of waters.
bibleSpine.gloss: The gospel is preached in a judgment-hour setting: fear God, give Him glory, worship the Creator — the message is present truth because the hour of His judgment is come.

bibleSpine.kjv: And the third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice, If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand,
bibleSpine.gloss: The third angel's warning against false worship stands over against the true worship of verse 7; the two loyalties are being sorted out in the judgment hour.

bibleSpine.kjv: Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.
bibleSpine.gloss: The three messages END by describing the PEOPLE they produce: a patient company marked by BOTH commandment-keeping AND the faith of Jesus — law and gospel held together, not law apart from gospel.

bibleSpine.kjv: And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.
bibleSpine.gloss: The same twofold mark identifies the remnant: keeping God's commandments and holding the testimony of Jesus — the object of the dragon's final war.

bibleSpine.kjv: And I fell at his feet to worship him. And he said unto me, See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren that have the testimony of Jesus: worship God: for the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.
bibleSpine.gloss: Scripture defines its own term: 'the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy' — the second mark of the remnant is self-interpreted within the book.

bibleSpine.kjv: To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne.
bibleSpine.gloss: Christ overcame by the same faith He now grants the saints; the overcomer sits where He sits — the faith 'of Jesus' is the faith BY which He Himself overcame, now offered to His people.

bibleSpine.kjv: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
bibleSpine.gloss: Jesus is not merely the object of faith but its author and finisher — He exercised faith Himself, enduring the cross; that same faith He originates and perfects in the saints.

bibleSpine.kjv: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
bibleSpine.gloss: 'The faith OF the Son of God' living in the believer — Christ's own faith reproduced in the saint, the very mechanism by which the crucified-with-Christ life is lived out in the flesh.

bibleSpine.kjv: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
bibleSpine.gloss: The gospel is God's saving POWER, not mere information — the everlasting gospel of Rev. 14:6 is this same power that actually saves the believer.

bibleSpine.kjv: For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.
bibleSpine.gloss: The gospel reveals a righteousness of God received by faith — this is righteousness by faith, which the pioneers and EGW identify as the third angel's message in verity.

bibleSpine.kjv: For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.
bibleSpine.gloss: Commandment-keeping is the fruit of love, not a burden set against the gospel — defining how 'they that keep the commandments' (Rev. 14:12) actually keep them.

bibleSpine.kjv: For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.
bibleSpine.gloss: The victory that overcomes the world IS faith — the same overcoming faith of Rev. 3:21 and 14:12, producing obedience in the born-again.

bibleSpine.kjv: If ye love me, keep my commandments.
bibleSpine.gloss: Christ's own order: love first, obedience following — the faith of Jesus working by love (1 John 5:3) produces the commandment-keeping of Rev. 14:12.

bibleSpine.kjv: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
bibleSpine.gloss: 'Fear God, and keep his commandments' — the identical two-fold call the first and third angels' messages sound (Rev. 14:7, 12), anchoring the judgment-hour message in the whole duty of man.

bibleSpine.kjv: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.
bibleSpine.gloss: The judgment setting of the message is not novel: 'God shall bring every work into judgment' — the hour of His judgment (Rev. 14:7) makes fear-God-and-keep-His-commandments present truth.

bibleSpine.kjv: A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.
bibleSpine.gloss: 'The judgment was set, and the books were opened' — the heavenly judgment scene whose hour has come (Rev. 14:7), the courtroom that makes the victory message urgent, ripening a people who can stand.

bibleSpine.kjv: Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.
bibleSpine.gloss: The book closes as chapter 14 described: the blessed are 'they that do his commandments' — the commandment-keeping people the three messages produce inherit the city.

symbolDefs.meaning: Not merely faith IN Jesus (though it includes trust in His ability to save fully) but the faith OF Jesus — the very faith by which Christ Himself overcame, now living in the saints. Scripture defines it: Christ overcame 'even as I also overcame' (Rev. 3:21) and grants the same to the overcomer; He is 'the author and finisher of our faith' who Himself endured by faith (Heb. 12:2); the believer's life is lived 'by the faith of the Son of God' living in him (Gal. 2:20); and this faith is 'the victory that overcometh the world' (1 John 5:4), producing commandment-keeping (Rev. 14:12; 1 John 5:3-4). In Rev. 14:12 it stands paired with, yet distinct from, 'the commandments of God' — the gospel half of the message that makes law-keeping possible.

The everlasting gospel (Rev. 14:6) in its judgment-hour form: righteousness by faith producing a commandment-keeping people. It is not law apart from gospel — the message ends by describing the people it makes, who keep BOTH 'the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus' (Rev. 14:9-12). Its warning against false worship (v. 9) is the counterpart to the call to worship the Creator (v. 7); its result is 'the patience of the saints' — a people ripened to stand in the judgment (Eccl. 12:13-14; Dan. 7:10). Righteousness by faith (Rom. 1:16-17) IS this message in verity, the faith of Jesus by which He overcame now living in the saints and yielding obedience.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Several have written to me, inquiring if the message of justification by faith is the third angel's message, and I have answered, "It is the third angel's message, in verity."
witnesses.gloss: The verity keystone: justification/righteousness by faith IS the third angel's message — confirming that Rev. 14:9-12 is gospel, not law apart from gospel, exactly as the section carries forward.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: "The faith of Jesus." It is talked of, but not understood. What constitutes the faith of Jesus, that belongs to the third angel's message? Jesus becoming our sin-bearer that He might become our sin-pardoning Saviour. He was treated as we deserve to be treated. He came to our world and took our sins that we might take His righteousness. And faith in the ability of Christ to save us amply and fully and entirely is the faith of Jesus.
witnesses.gloss: EGW defines the very symbol this section owns — 'the faith of Jesus' that belongs to the third angel's message — as trust in Christ's full ability to save, grounded in the great exchange (He took our sins, we take His righteousness).

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: The messages of this chapter constitute a threefold warning which is to prepare the inhabitants of the earth for the Lord's second coming... The result of an acceptance of these messages is given in the word: "Here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus." In order to be prepared for the judgment, it is necessary that men should keep the law of God. That law will be the standard of character in the judgment.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms the section's spine: the three messages END by describing the people they produce (Rev. 14:12), and the judgment-hour setting makes the message present truth that must ripen a people who can stand.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: We have been given a work of most solemn import—the proclamation of the first, second, and third angels' messages. The subject of the first angel's message is the everlasting gospel, and its burden is the warning, The end of all things is at hand.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms 'the subject of the first angel's message is the everlasting gospel' (Rev. 14:6) — the gospel is the substance the judgment-hour messages carry.

witnesses.author: Uriah Smith
witnesses.quote: We have already briefly spoken of the commandments of God; a few words should be devoted to the faith of Jesus. This term is used in distinction from the commandments of God... That this is the sense in which it is used in Revelation 14:12, is further evident from the fact that it is spoken of as being kept in the same manner that the commandments of God are kept.
witnesses.gloss: Pioneer symbol-owner (Uriah Smith) works out 'the faith of Jesus' in Rev. 14:12 as distinct from, yet kept alongside, the commandments of God — the gospel half paired with the law half.

witnesses.author: Uriah Smith
witnesses.quote: The chronology of this message seems to be distinctly marked by the fact that it is given in the period of the "patience of the saints," which follows the proclamation of the two former messages. "Here is the patience of the saints; here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus." ... And this period of the saints' patience is marked by a most important fact, viz., the keeping of the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms that the third message is identified by the PEOPLE it produces — a patient company keeping the commandments and the faith of Jesus — the section's central claim.

witnesses.author: Uriah Smith
witnesses.quote: A second cause, and one, too, which should not be lightly passed over, is this; The preaching of the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus. This is the cause of the conflict between the dragon and the last fragment of the church... It is because the saints are keeping all the commandments of God that the dragon makes war upon them.
witnesses.gloss: Links Rev. 14:12 to Rev. 12:17 — the commandment-keeping, faith-of-Jesus people are the very remnant the dragon wars against, tying the two twofold-marked companies together.

witnesses.author: Joseph Bates
witnesses.quote: We were also greatly cheered and strengthened by the light which we received on the subject of the three angels' messages of Revelation 14:6-12... the third giving a most solemn warning against false worship, and presenting the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.
witnesses.gloss: Historical witness that the earliest Sabbatarian Adventists (Bates) identified the third angel's message as presenting 'the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus' — the doctrinal foundation of the movement.

historyAnchor: The Sabbatarian Adventist pioneers (Joseph Bates, later systematized by Uriah Smith in The Three Messages of Revelation 14:6-12) fixed this reading from the late 1840s onward, and Ellen White's 1888/1890 statements identified righteousness by faith as the third angel's message in verity.
uncertainties: The local corpus surfaced Uriah Smith (TMR) and EGW abundantly, but did not return searchable hits for Waggoner's CHR/GTI or A. T. Jones's LOF under the queries tried; the pioneer confirmation here rests on Smith and Bates rather than Waggoner/Jones, though the righteousness-by-faith framing is anchored by EGW's 1SM 372.2.

'The faith of Jesus' has two complementary senses in the witnesses: EGW (3SM 172.3) stresses faith in Christ's ability to save; Uriah Smith (TMR 134.2) reads it as the precepts/doctrines of the gospel 'kept' like the commandments. The section's own framing (the faith BY which Jesus overcame, per Rev. 3:21 / Heb. 12:2 / Gal. 2:20) is a third, Scripture-grounded sense that harmonizes both but is developed here primarily from the Bible spine rather than an explicit pioneer statement of that exact phrasing.
